title: Surface Spec v1
description: The machine statement of PROPOSAL-ui-oracle-loop.md §4.2: how one surface — a feature area with its own routes and controls — is supposed to function. This file declares STRUCTURE only. The cross-field invariants (§4.5 I1-I8: 'every route has a back unless it is the root', 'behaviors cover visible_in', 'outage.must_show and empty.must_show are disjoint', hit_rect reciprocity) are implemented in code by `aof-tools ui spec validate`, not encoded here — a schema that half-expresses a rule gives it two homes and lets them drift. JSON has no comments, so every `description` in this file IS its documentation.

id.description: §4.2: all ids are lower-case, dot- and hyphen-separated. A control id MUST equal the widget's semantics identifier.

idList.description: A list of ids resolved against this spec (or, for route entries, another spec in the same repo).

effect.description: §7.5: the machine-classifiable effect classes, read off the before/after diff of one activation. `navigation` = route changed; `toggle` = announced state flipped; `select` = selection node changed; `dialog` = new modal node; `submit` = request + result node; `inert` = zero delta.

whenClause.description: §4.3: the observed pre-activation state a behaviour applies to. `when` clauses on one control are mutually exclusive and together cover every state in `visible_in`; the probe resolves the active behaviour from the state it observes.

contentContract.description: §4.4: the content contract for one state — literal strings that must or must not be on screen, or a prose `rule` for the cases a string match cannot express. `{placeholder}` braces are resolved from the seed.

hitRect.description: §4.2 / §4.5 I6: the DECLARED hit-target intent. Overlap itself is not statically checkable and is not checked — the spec declares intent, the probe measures rects (§7.5 `disjoint`, `hit-target`, `within`). The static check is resolvability and consistency only.

max.description: An upper bound on the control's rect, `WxH` in logical pixels, that the probe asserts. Not a layout instruction.

within.description: This control sits inside the named control's area but MUST own its own hit target — the declarable form of the aodex#544 defect, where a chevron's semantics node spanned the whole 360px row. Resolves to a control in this spec, and must not also appear in this control's `disjoint_from`.

disjoint_from.description: Controls whose rects must not overlap this one's. Reciprocal: both controls name each other, and neither names itself.

behavior.description: §4.3: one state-conditional behaviour of a control. A UI may support several behaviours for one control, never two for the same observed state.

does.description: What activating the control does, in one sentence, for the reader of the spec.

effect.description: The effect classes this activation is allowed to produce (§7.5 `effect`).

must_not.description: §4.3: negations drawn from must_not_vocabulary.json. Free text needs `manual: true`, which keeps the item on the human-verify list.

entry.description: §4.5 I2: at least one declared way in. An element is either `{control: <id>}` or a literal entry kind such as `deeplink`.

back.description: §4.5 I2: required unless the route declares `root: true`. `target` is the route landed on; `via` lists the back affordances that must work (§7.5 `route-back`).

root.description: §4.5 I2: this route is the declared root and therefore needs no `back`.

guards.description: §4.5 I8: each guard names the denied state it renders.

reachable_from_nav.description: §4.2: false requires a `justification` (aodex#517 — four screens unreachable).

title.description: §4.2 / §7.5 `title`: every route has a visible title. `{placeholder}` braces are resolved from the seed.

control.description: §4.3: `controls[]` is the interaction contract. Either one `does` + `effect` pair, or a `behaviors[]` list whose `when` clauses are exclusive and cover `visible_in`.

id.description: MUST equal the semantics identifier the widget publishes — this is what the probe looks the control up by.

kind.description: §4.2: the control kind, which selects the pattern defaults it inherits (§4.5 I5).

visible_in.description: §4.5 I3: the states this control is on screen in. A subset of `states[].id`.

must_not.description: §4.3: applies to EVERY behaviour of this control. Terms from must_not_vocabulary.json.

activation.description: §4.2 (amended): a MAP, not a list. `pointer` is a boolean; `keyboard` lists the keys that must activate the control (§7.5 `keyboard-complete`).

disabled_when.description: §4.3: null, or a condition together with the reason SHOWN to the user. There is no honestly-non-functional control without a surfaced reason (§7.5 `no-op`).

a11y.description: §4.2: the semantics role and the state changes the control announces.

destructive.description: §4.3: true requires `confirm` naming the dialog control.

state.description: §4.4: every surface declares at minimum populated, empty, error, outage, long-content, narrow and dark; `loading` when the surface owns an async fetch. Every state has a seed.

seed.description: §7.4: the seed profile the e2e entrypoint honours.

as.description: §7.4: the identity from the e2e identity set. Default: the primary user.

ref.description: §8.3: the locked render this state is judged against, as `<kind>/<file>` (e.g. `locked/populated.png`) relative to the directory passed as `aof-tools ui sheet --refs <dir>`. The FIRST path segment is the reference kind and is what labels the ref pane on the sheet — one of `mockup`, `donor`, `locked`; any other first segment leaves `ref_kind: null`. The top-level `references` block is NOT the resolution root — nothing reads it — so a path written relative to the paths it names comes back `ref_status: MISSING` with `ref_kind: null` on every row.

fault.description: §7.4: the injected fault that produces this state (a 500, a dependency 503).

flow.description: §4.5 I7: every step references existing controls and routes, and the flow ends in a `back` or a declared terminal route.

scopeRule.description: §4.6: what resets or is invalidated on a scope event. The planner derives provider-invalidation tests from these; the crawl fires each event and checks the list (§10.1, §7.5 `scope-reset`).

schema_version.description: §4.5 I1: the spec's schema version, checked against the engine's supported range. Absent means 1.

surface.description: §4.1: unique within the repo. One spec per navigation destination group — in practice one per `lib/features/<x>/`.

patterns.description: §4.5 I5: pattern-library ids from the pinned eden-ui-flutter release. A control of a pattern kind inherits that pattern's `must_not` defaults and may not silently drop them.

references.description: §4.1: where the mockup, the donor captures (completeness only) and the look-locked renders live, relative to the spec. DOCUMENTATION FOR A HUMAN — no module reads these three paths. `aof-tools ui sheet --refs <dir>` is what resolves a `state.ref`, and that directory is the one holding the `mockup/`, `donor/` and `locked/` subdirectories these keys name.

design_read.description: §5 / design-craft §1-2: the design read recorded once per surface rather than once per SUMMARY.

acceptance.description: §4.1 re-lock rule: any change to `routes`, `controls` or `states` CLEARS `locked_sheet`. Phase B refuses to run a judge against a surface whose lock is cleared.

locked_sheet.description: The sha256 of the approved review sheet.

locked_shape_hash.description: TRD 34-07. The sha256 of the canonical JSON of `{routes, controls, states}` ONLY — the three keys §4.1's re-lock rule names. Deliberately NOT over the whole front matter: if a `design_read` rewording cleared the lock, the team would learn to re-approve without reading, which is worse than no lock. `aof-tools ui lock` writes it; `ui spec validate` compares it to report `lock: held | cleared`. An `acceptance` block WITHOUT it reports `lock: MISSING` — never `held`.

locked_section_hashes.description: TRD 34-07. One hash per §4.1 key, as at the lock. Stored rather than recomputed because telling routes-changed from states-changed after the fact is impossible without the values at lock time — and `lock: cleared` with no named section sends a human back to diff the file by hand. Optional: a hand-written lock without them still resolves held/cleared, and the reason says the section cannot be named.
